title: Slept in My Lenses

patient.name: Mr Lim Jun Wei
patient.presenting_complaint: One painful red eye with blurred vision and light sensitivity, wears contact lenses

history.hpc: Mr Lim says 'My right eye very pain and blur, cannot see the light also. I wear contact lens, sometimes I sleep with it never take out.' One eye, painful, watery, photophobic, getting worse since yesterday.
history.pmhx: Wears monthly soft contact lenses; admits overnight wear and topping up old solution.
history.social_hx: Student, long hours, frequent contact lens overwear.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Right eye markedly red with watering; cornea to be examined urgently by the doctor

investigations.history_and_triage: Focused history identifies a painful, photophobic red eye with reduced vision in a contact lens wearer who overwears and sleeps in lenses — a high-risk picture for microbial keratitis.
investigations.red_flags_checked: Pain, photophobia, reduced vision and contact lens use are all red flags.
investigations.triage_category: Urgent — escalate promptly for same-day doctor assessment; this is not a routine red eye.

diagnosis: A painful, photophobic red eye with reduced vision in a contact lens overwearer is a high-risk presentation for microbial keratitis. The PSA recognises the red flags, escalates urgently for doctor assessment, and advises the patient to stop lens wear. No medical diagnosis is made by the PSA.

immediate: Confirm identity and take a focused red-eye history including contact lens habits
Identify the red flags: pain, photophobia, reduced vision and contact lens overwear
Record visual acuity for both eyes
Escalate urgently for same-day doctor review rather than routine queueing
Advise the patient to stop wearing the lens and bring the lens/case if available
follow_up: Urgent doctor assessment with slit lamp examination
Keep the patient from rubbing or further lens wear while waiting
patient_education: Explain that sleeping in lenses and reusing solution raises infection risk
Advise stopping lens wear until reviewed
Stress the importance of being seen quickly to protect vision
